title: Philly Joe Jones - Wikipedia
notes: Joseph Rudolph "Philly" Joe Jones, born 15 July 1923, died 30 August 1985. 'Philly' for Philadelphia, to tell him from Papa Jo Jones. A tap dancer on WIP's Kiddie Show as a child; US Army in the war; house drummer at Cafe Society in New York from 1947 (Tadd Dameron). The Miles Davis Quintet 1955-58 with Red Garland, John Coltrane and Paul Chambers; Davis's favourite drummer, as he was Bill Evans's. A leader from 1958; with Bill Evans and Hank Mobley. London and Paris 1967-72 (Archie Shepp, Mal Waldron, Hank Mobley); taught in Hampstead 1967-69; Mo' Joe (1968). Toured with Evans 1976 and 1978; Galaxy records 1977-79; Red Garland 1977; founded Dameronia 1981.

title: Todd Bishop, 'Key players: Philly Joe Jones' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 30 January 2021)
notes: 'the strongest, clearest voice playing modern bop in the 50s'; 'He seems to have wrapped up and finished a lot things created by Max Roach, Kenny Clarke, and Art Blakey'; clean, 'everything is lined up'; 'edgier, with a very substantive, deep R&B sound'; 'snare drum oriented, and rudiment oriented, with a rather crusty sound on the snare drum'; Charley Wilcoxon's books; 'a really polished brush technique'; 'His cymbal beat is fairly straight, with a solid quarter note pulse— with an emphasis on the skip note when playing in 2'; a 22-inch bass drum, 13- and 16-inch toms, often a 20-inch ride.

title: Todd Bishop, 'Transcription: Philly Joe Jones - Gaza Strip' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 7 July 2025), PDF
notes: Lee Morgan, Indeed! The eight-bar drum intro, the figure at the top of the solos (0:43), his comping under Morgan's five choruses (2:36), at 222. 'punctuations with the bass drum on 4, followed by a snare drum accent on the & of 1'; at phrase ends 'the & of 2/& of 4'; the top of a solo 'the one strongly, followed by some big accents off of a dotted-quarter rhythm'; six-stroke rolls in the intro.

title: Todd Bishop, 'Philly Joe plays an entrance: Oleo' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 19 November 2014)
notes: Relaxin'. His entrance with sticks on Coltrane's second chorus: a snare lead-in in straight eighths, 'punches on 1 and 4 at the top of a chorus', lighter accents after; the hi-hat 'sporadically'. Half note = 138 on the image.

title: Todd Bishop, 'Philly Joe starts a chorus: The Theme' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 2 December 2014)
notes: Miles (The New Miles Davis Quintet). The roll out of the bass solo, the crash on 1, accents around beat 4; the hi-hat steady from bar 3, 'an arrangement element'. 165.

title: Todd Bishop, 'Transcription: Philly Joe Jones - Locomotion' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 31 March 2013), PDF
notes: Blue Train. The drum intro, 'Fast bop', with stickings; bars 5-8 simplified with accented doubles.

title: Todd Bishop, 'Groove o' the day: Philly Joe Afro 6' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 17 July 2019)
notes: Sonny Rollins, Newk's Time, Asiatic Raes: two bars of 6/8 at dotted quarter 108; the bell, a rim click on 2, the bass drum on 1 and 4, the floor tom on 5 and 6; 'no small tom'.

title: Todd Bishop, 'Transcription: Philly Joe Jones - Gone' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 29 March 2020), PDF
notes: Miles Davis, Porgy and Bess. The whole track but the trumpet solo; 'that Philly Joe beat, with the rim click on 4'; 205 rising to 240.

title: Todd Bishop, 'Transcription: Philly Joe brush feature' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 6 December 2019), PDF
notes: Chet Baker in New York, Soft Winds: his 24-bar brush solo after 4:30, at 115; a tremolo with one hand and accents with the other (bar 5); the brush laid on the head and rolled with the palm (bars 17-19).

title: Todd Bishop, 'Philly Joe kicks and set ups' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 1 February 2021), PDF
notes: Soft Winds' head in and out at 123: the band's figures and his set-ups; a straight-eighth lick, stick shots, chokes. Read; not used for a song (its mixed sixteenths and triplets were not read bar by bar).

title: Todd Bishop, 'Transcription: Philly Joe trading' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 1 October 2023), PDF
notes: Everybody Digs Bill Evans, Minority: his breaks from 2:51 at 247; 'No tom toms at all here, just snare drum, bass drum, a cymbal, and hihats. A lot of stick shots'; 'much of it is linear'.

title: Todd Bishop, 'Transcription: Philly Joe Jones - Let's Cool One' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 29 July 2019), PDF
notes: Clark Terry, In Orbit: his solo at 136, 'a rather old fashioned way of soloing, with a lot of rudimental activity played on the snare drum, while the feet keep time'; 'Jones mostly plays the hihat on 2 and 4 and feathers quarter notes on the bass drum throughout'. Read; not used for a song (its sixteenths and triplets mixed in one bar fit no grid here).

title: Todd Bishop, 'Know your tempos: Workin', Steamin', Cookin', Relaxin'' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 19 May 2023)
notes: The tempo of every track on the four 1956 Prestige records; Oleo 258.

title: Todd Bishop, 'Philly Joe's early career' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 12 March 2022), quoting Rick Mattingly's 1982 Modern Drummer interview
notes: Jones: rhythm-and-blues bands on arriving in New York, Joe Morris's with Johnny Griffin, Elmo Hope and Percy Heath, 'for 3 or 4 years'; Tiny Grimes's Highlanders; Bull Moose Jackson; Arnett Cobb.

title: Philly Joe Jones on European television, late 1960s (YouTube fIPIc3bkYoc)
notes: Black and white, a trio with piano and bass: a short rounded natural, a moustache, a dark jacket over an open white shirt, a patterned scarf; a pale kit with chrome hardware. The likeness.
